text.text: Check in each day, see the week fill up, and watch the habits that stick. Add a check-in to the log below.
Check in
Progress by habit
Habits
Month view
Paused habits
Do this once a week, ten minutes, at the same time. The misses below are your data, not your report card.
Ten minutes every Sunday keeps the system honest.
Look back
Open the calendar view and note which days were empty
Find the habit with the most missed days
Check whether a paused habit deserves another try
Look ahead
Pick one habit to make easier this week
Decide where each habit fits in the day
Archive anything you no longer care about
This week
How to read your misses
A miss on one habit only: the habit is probably too big or sits at the wrong time of day.
Misses across every habit on one weekday: that day needs a lighter plan, not more willpower.
A run of misses after a disruption (travel, illness): restart with the two-minute version.
Small and specific beats ambitious and vague.
Rules of thumb
Start with a habit that takes two minutes.
Attach it to something you already do every day.
Never miss twice in a row.
Track the habit, not your mood about it.
A habit you can do on your worst day is a habit you will keep.
Frequency choices

It is a chore or a long session

text.text: A worked example

Habit: stretch for five minutes. Cue: right after brushing teeth. Minimum version: touch your toes once. Reward: a glass of water. After four weeks the Completion column shows whether it stuck; below 50 percent, shrink it rather than quitting.
Setting up your own
Add the habit with its cue and a minutes-per-day number that is honest.
Check in on the Habit log every day, even for misses. Honest misses make the completion figure useful.
Review Completion and This month (%) each week and change one thing.
